title: GEPCO Bill Calculator 2026 (Latest Tariff) | Wattlyst
meta: Estimate your GEPCO bill from units with the 2026 NEPRA slabs, fixed charge, QTA, GST and the latest NEPRA FPA. What one unit over a slab costs.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: What is the GEPCO per unit rate?
p: GEPCO bills the uniform A-1 domestic tariff that NEPRA determined and the Government notified for 2026; the company sets none of the rates itself. An unprotected home in Gujranwala, Sialkot, Gujrat, Narowal, Hafizabad, Mandi Bahauddin or Wazirabad pays the rate of the slab its monthly units reach on every unit: 250 units are all billed at Rs 33.10. Protected consumers pay two low rates slab by slab, and lifeline consumers less again.

The table below is built around the slab edges, so you can see what one unit over a boundary does to the bill. The worked examples follow one home through a protected month, the month it loses protection, a normal month and a month further up the slabs.

sections.h2: GEPCO tariff: what one unit over a slab costs
p: Unprotected domestic slabs are 100 units wide, and the rate of the slab reached applies to every unit of the month, not just the units above the line. So a month of 210 units is billed at Rs 33.10 on all of them and costs Rs 10,054, while a protected month of 190 units costs Rs 3,558. The gap between those two bills is the price of a few units of extra use at the wrong time.

The same thing happens at every edge further up: in the table, compare the row just under a boundary with the row just over it. If a month looks like it will land a few units into the next slab, moving a wash, an iron session or a pump run to after the reading date keeps the whole month in the lower slab.

sections.h2: How do I read my GEPCO bill before estimating it?
p: Three printed items feed this calculator. The units are the difference between the current and previous meter readings shown on the bill. The sanctioned load, in kW, is in the connection details and sets the fixed charge. The category line shows whether the bill was worked out as protected, unprotected or lifeline. The FPA, the fuel price adjustment for the month, is a per-unit line that changes monthly; copy it into the advanced field for the exact figure.

Also check the reading dates. A cycle longer than a month carries more units than a normal month and can push you over a slab edge; the bill audit tool works out the thirty-day equivalent and whether the slab was fair.

sections.h2: GEPCO bill estimate vs the official bill check
p: This GEPCO bill estimate works from the figures you type and does not fetch your account. The official bill, with the reference number, due date, arrears and the exact FPA, is on the GEPCO website, which links the duplicate bill on the PITC portal; enter the reference number from the top of an earlier bill, digits only, without the spaces printed between groups.

Use the estimate to understand what each printed line should be, to plan the next month, or to see whether a bill that looks high is explained by the slab it reached. Every bill also carries an FPA line; see what the FPA line on your bill means. A home on a time-of-use meter can check the peak hours for GEPCO.
Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sialkot, Narowal, Hafizabad, Mandi Bahauddin and Wazirabad, from its head office in Gujranwala. If your bill carries another company's name, use that company's calculator instead.

faq.q: How do I get a GEPCO bill estimate from my units?
faq.a: Enter the units and the sanctioned load from the bill, tick protected only if the bill prints that category, and replace the pre-filled FPA with the one on your bill under advanced settings. For 250 units the estimate is Rs 11,892, FPA included.

faq.q: What is the GEPCO per unit rate for a home?
faq.a: The uniform NEPRA domestic slab rate for the slab the month reaches: Rs 33.10 per unit for an unprotected home using 250 units. The table above gives the rate on each side of every slab edge; protected and lifeline consumers pay less.

faq.q: Is the GEPCO tariff different from LESCO or IESCO?
faq.a: No. The 2026 tariff notified as SRO 279(I)/2026 is uniform for all ex-WAPDA DISCOs and K-Electric. NEPRA sets one FPA for every DISCO too, so a GEPCO bill for the same units equals a LESCO bill; real bills differ only by billing days, arrears and local items.

faq.q: How do I check my GEPCO bill online?
faq.a: The GEPCO website links a duplicate bill page on the PITC portal; enter the reference number printed at the top of an earlier bill, digits only, to see the current bill and due date. This calculator estimates the bill from units; it does not fetch your account.

GEPCO supplies Gujranwala, Sialkot, Gujrat, Narowal, Hafizabad and Mandi Bahauddin. Faults and billing complaints go to the national electricity helpline 118 (call, or SMS 8118); the official bill, with its reference number, is on the GEPCO website.

faq.q: What happens when a GEPCO bill goes one unit over the slab?
faq.a: Every unit of the month is billed at the higher slab's rate, and the fixed charge per kW also steps up. In the table, compare the rows just under and just over each hundred-unit line to see the jump.

faq.q: Why does my GEPCO bill differ from this estimate?
faq.a: The estimate uses the pre-filled FPA unless you enter your bill's, and it cannot see arrears, late payment surcharge or meter rent. If the reading dates cover more than a month, the units may have crossed a slab because of the long cycle; run the bill audit tool.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over Rs 25,000?
faq.a: Usually because of advance income tax, which this estimate leaves out: a domestic consumer not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more. Who pays the income tax line is explained with the electricity bill calculator.

l.t: Who pays the income tax line

key_facts: GEPCO, the Gujranwala Electric Power Company, supplies Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sialkot, Narowal, Hafizabad, Mandi Bahauddin and Wazirabad from its head office in Gujranwala and bills the uniform NEPRA A-1 domestic tariff for 2026, not a tariff of its own.
An unprotected GEPCO consumer using 250 units pays Rs 33.10 on every unit, which is Rs 8,275 of energy charge before the fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA and GST.

Crossing a slab costs more than the extra units: 190 protected units cost about Rs 3,558, while 210 unprotected units, only a few more, cost about Rs 10,054 because the whole month moves to the unprotected rate of Rs 33.10.
Protection on GEPCO needs every one of the last 6 bills at or under 200 units on a connection below 5 kW; a single bill over the limit ends it for the next 6 months.
GST at 18% is charged on the energy charge, fixed charge and surcharges together and adds Rs 1,814 to a 250 unit GEPCO bill; the surcharge and GST defaults are secondary-source figures that change.

The bill jumps at 700 units: up to there every unit is billed at Rs 41.85, but one unit more moves all of them to the top slab rate of Rs 47.20, which adds Rs 4,481 to the bill of an unprotected 1 kW home.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more; consumers on the list pay none.
mistakes: Looking for a GEPCO tariff of its own. GEPCO bills the uniform NEPRA domestic slabs; only the monthly FPA is specific to the month.
Thinking only the units above a slab line are charged at the higher rate. For unprotected homes the rate of the slab reached applies to every unit of the month.
Ticking protected because the bill was low this month. Protection needs all of the last 6 bills at or under 200 units, and one month over ends it.
Ignoring the reading dates. A long cycle carries extra units that can cross a slab edge; check the thirty-day equivalent before assuming the meter is wrong.

fields.label: Units on the GEPCO bill
fields.hint: Units (kWh) for the month: the difference between this and last month's meter readings, or the units line on the bill.

fields.name: sanctioned_kw
fields.label: Sanctioned load
fields.hint: The kW printed in the connection details of the GEPCO bill. It sets the fixed charge. A connection of 5 kW or more is billed on peak and off-peak (ToU) rates instead: use the ToU bill calculator.

fields.name: protected
fields.label: Protected consumer
fields.hint: Tick only if the bill prints the protected category; it needs six months in a row under the limit.

fields.name: lifeline
fields.label: Lifeline consumer (up to one hundred units)
fields.hint: Only for very small consumers whose bill shows the lifeline category.

fields.name: period
fields.label: Billing quarter for QTA
fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment depends on the quarter the bill falls in.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit
fields.label: FC surcharge
fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from the bill. Secondary-source default.
fields.placeholder: Blank = Rs 3.23 per unit (none on lifeline or protected)

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FPA
fields.hint: Pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified fuel adjustment, the one for July 2026 charged on September 2026 bills. October 2026 bills carry Rs 1.11 per unit for August 2026, reported in the news; this page keeps the latest NEPRA-verified rate until that decision is published. Replace it with the FPA rate printed on your bill (negative is a credit). Protected homes pay it too; lifeline bills carry none.

fields.name: fpa_units
fields.label: Units in the FPA month
fields.hint: NEPRA charges the FPA on the units of the month it adjusts (the FPA month, usually two months before this bill), not on this month's units. Copy that month's units from the units history on your bill. Blank = this month's units.

fields.name: gst_pct
fields.label: GST
fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal.

content.answer: A GEPCO home in Gujranwala, Sialkot or Gujrat using 250 units in a month as an unprotected consumer on a 1 kW connection pays about Rs 11,892: Rs 8,275 energy charge at Rs 33.10 per unit, plus fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA, the July 2026 FPA and GST. GEPCO bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + surcharges, then GST on the subtotal.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = rate of the band the month's units reach (unprotected) or slab-wise (protected)
fixed = Rs per kW of the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC, QTA, FPA = per-unit surcharges printed on the GEPCO bill
